summary:
[  edit  ]
The Point File In  TOP  loads 3D point data into TOPs from either a single file or a sequence of files. Points are composed of one or more floating point values such as XYZ positions, RGB color values, 3D normals, scanner intensity, etc. The Point File in  TOP  will load all available point data, but only four channels can be placed into the output image. By default, the first four point data channels are placed into the red, green, blue and alpha channels respectively; however, you can assign any point channel to a colour channel using the parameters on the Point Data page. Attach a  Point File Select TOP  to create additional output images from the same source file.
The Point File In  TOP  will read point data from various mesh and floating point data files including:  .obj ,  .ply ,  .fits  (astronomy format), and  .exr . It can also load ASCII point files ( .xyz ,  .pts ,  .csv ,  .txt , etc) with one point per line and comma or space separated fields. The first line in ASCII point files can either be the number of points, the names of the point fields or the first point in the file.
For a complete list, see  File Types . The  OpenEXR  file format is generally best to use as it is binary, can be read in multi-frame file sequences that uses TouchDesigner's movie file pre-reading and buffering, and can be written from TouchDesigner's  Movie File Out TOP  with unlimited numbers of channels.
Examine the state of a Point File In  TOP  by attaching an  Info CHOP . This will show information like the number of points, fields per point and the number of frames. It also shows dynamic information like the file open status, current frame, readahead frames and queue size, dropped frame count, CPU decode time and  GPU  upload time.
Headers : If the file contains any additional header data, this can be viewed by attaching an  Info DAT . Header data is stored as key-value pairs with the keys in the first column and the corresponding data in the second column, which can easily be interpreted with python.
All of the ASCII point list formats are loaded the same way whether their extention is  txt ,  csv ,  xyz , etc.  The parser looks for the first separating character (comma, space or tab) and then uses that to delimit the rest of the file. It will ignore delimiters that are inside single or double quotes. There are a few special rules depending on the delimiter style e.g. multiple spaces are merged together, but a comma at the end of a line indicates a blank field afterwards. Once a delimiter is established, The first line can be the number of points, but it is ignored. If the next line are strings then it is treated as a row of headers (channel names). Each row after that is considered a point.
See also  OpenEXR .

parameters.label: File
parameters.name: file
parameters.description: The path and name of the point file to load. Point file formats are those found in  File Types .  You can specify files on the internet using  http://  ...

parameters.label: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="ISO

parameters.label: Reload
parameters.name: reload
parameters.description: Change from 0 to 1 to force the file to reload. Useful when the file changes or did not exist at first.

parameters.label: Reload  Pulse
parameters.name: reloadpulse
parameters.description: Immediately reload the point data file.

parameters.label: Red
parameters.name: red
parameters.description: ⊞  - Select one of the available point data channels to place it into the red channel of the output image. Selecting One or Zero will place the constance value into the output channel.

parameters.label: Green
parameters.name: green
parameters.description: ⊞  - Select one of the available point data channels to place it into the green channel of the output image. Selecting One or Zero will place the constance value into the output channel.

parameters.label: Blue
parameters.name: blue
parameters.description: ⊞  - Select one of the available point data channels to place it into the blue channel of the output image. Selecting One or Zero will place the constance value into the output channel.

parameters.label: Alpha
parameters.name: alpha
parameters.description: ⊞  - Select one of the available point data channels to place it into the alpha channel of the output image. Selecting One or Zero will place the constance value into the output channel.

parameters.label: Play Mode
parameters.name: playmode
parameters.description: ⊞  - Specifies the method used to play the animation, there are 3 options.

parameters.label: Locked to  Timeline
parameters.name: locked
parameters.description: This mode locks the animation to the timeline. Scrubbing or jumping in the timeline will change the animation position accordingly. The parameters Play, Reset, Speed, and Index are disabled in this mode since the timeline is directly tied to  position.

parameters.label: Specify Index
parameters.name: specify
parameters.description: This mode allows the user to specify a particular position in the animation using the Index parameter below. Use this mode for random access to any location in the movie.

parameters.label: Sequential
parameters.name: sequential
parameters.description: This mode continually plays regardless of the timeline position (the Index parameter is disabled). Reset and Speed parameters below are enabled to allow some control.

parameters.label: Play
parameters.name: play
parameters.description: Animation plays when 1, stops when 0.

parameters.label: Speed
parameters.name: speed
parameters.description: This is a speed multiplier which only works when Play Mode is  Sequential . A value of 1 is the default playback speed. A value of 2 is double speed, 0.5 is half speed and so on. Negative values will play the animation backwards.

parameters.label: Cue
parameters.name: cue
parameters.description: Jumps to Cue Point when set to 1. Only available when Play Mode is Sequential.

parameters.label: Cue  Pulse
parameters.name: cuepulse
parameters.description: Instantly jumps to the Cue Point position in the movie.

parameters.label: Cue  Point
parameters.name: cuepoint
parameters.description: Set any index in the animation as a point to jump to.

parameters.label: Cue Point Unit
parameters.name: cuepointunit
parameters.description: ⊞  - Select the units for this parameter from Index, Frames, Seconds, and Fraction (percentage).

parameters.label: Cue Behavior
parameters.name: cuebehavior
parameters.description: ⊞  - Customize the Cue parameter's behavior.

parameters.label: On Release, Repeat Cued  Frame
parameters.name: repeat
parameters.description: When releasing the Cue parameter, immediately play the next frame.

parameters.label: On Release, Play Next  Frame
parameters.name: play
parameters.description: When releasing the Cue parameter, first play the cued frame before continuing to play the next frame.

parameters.label: Index
parameters.name: index
parameters.description: This parameter explicitly sets the file sequence position when Play Mode is set to Specify Index. The units menu on the right lets you specify the index in the following units: Index, Frames, Seconds, and Fraction (percentage). For example, assume you have a sequence that internally is 25 fps, and the timeline that is 60 fps. If you set Units to Index and the parameter value to 25, you get the image that is 1 second into the sequence. If you set the Units to Frames and set the value to 60 you get the same image at 1 second into the movie.

parameters.label: Index Unit
parameters.name: indexunit
parameters.description: ⊞  - Select the units for this parameter from Index, Frames, Seconds, and Fraction (percentage).

parameters.label: Loop Crossfade
parameters.name: loopcrossfade
parameters.description: Crossfades the beginning and end of the animation together to create a smooth transition when looping. If the movie uses Trim options, it will crossfade Trim Start with Trim End positions.

parameters.label: Loop Crossfade Unit
parameters.name: loopcrossfadeunit
parameters.description: ⊞  - Select the units for this parameter from Index, Frames, Seconds, and Fraction (percentage).

parameters.label: Step Size
parameters.name: stepsize
parameters.description: Sets how many frames to skip before displaying next frame. For example, a StepSize of 30 will display every 30th frame. The timing of the animation playback does not change, so with a Step Size of 30 and a sample rate of 30, a new frame will be displayed every second.

parameters.label: Audio Loop
parameters.name: audioloop
parameters.description: ⊞  - This menu helps you determine how to treat the audio as the end of an animation approaches. This is needed because in some cases of playing an animation, like when driving with an index, the  TOP  will not know if you intend to loop it or not.

parameters.label: Silence
parameters.name: silence
parameters.description: Audio will go silent when the animation ends.

parameters.label: Fade
parameters.name: fade
parameters.description: Audio will fade out when the animation ends.

parameters.label: Image Sequence Indexing
parameters.name: imageindexing
parameters.description: ⊞  - Determines how a file sequence is ordered.

parameters.label: Zero Based
parameters.name: zero
parameters.description: Index the sequence of files starting at 0, after sorting them alphanumerically.

parameters.label: Filename Based
parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: Index the sequence of files using the numbers on the end of the filenames. I.e a file named flower400.obj will be frame index 400, regardless of if there are other files in the directory before it.

parameters.label: Interpolate Frames
parameters.name: interp
parameters.description: Interpolates between frames based based on exact time. For example, if the index (in frames) is 1.5, then frames 1 and 2 will be blended 50-50. If the index is 1.7 then 30% of frame 1 is blended with 70% of frame 2 and so on.

parameters.label: Loading/Error Image
parameters.name: loadingerrorimage
parameters.description: ⊞  - When the file can not be loaded for some reason, select what to display instead.

parameters.label: Trim
parameters.name: trim
parameters.description: Enables the parameters below to set trim in and out points.

parameters.label: Trim Start
parameters.name: tstart
parameters.description: Trim the starting point of the movie.

parameters.label: Trim Start Unit
parameters.name: tstartunit
parameters.description: ⊞  - Select the units for this parameter from Index, Frames, Seconds, and Fraction (percentage).

parameters.label: Trim End
parameters.name: tend
parameters.description: Trim the ending point of the movie.

parameters.label: Trim End Unit
parameters.name: tendunit
parameters.description: ⊞  - Select the units for this parameter from Index, Frames, Seconds, and Fraction (percentage).

parameters.label: Extend Left
parameters.name: textendleft
parameters.description: ⊞  - Determines how the Point File In  TOP  handles animation positions that lie before the Trim Start position. For example, if Trim Start is set to 1, and the animation's current index is -10, the Extend Left menu determines how the animation position is calculated.

parameters.label: Hold
parameters.name: hold
parameters.description: Displays the first frame in the animation range (the frame specified by Trim Start) for any position before Trim Start.

parameters.label: Cycle
parameters.name: cycle
parameters.description: Loops the movie range continuously.

parameters.label: Mirror
parameters.name: mirror
parameters.description: Loops the animation range in a zig-zag pattern. For example, playing backwards from Trim Start the animation will index will climb towards Trim End, at which point is will decend down towards Trim Start again and continue to zig-zag (or mirror) the further the animation plays backwards.

parameters.label: Black
parameters.name: black
parameters.description: Displays black frame for any animation position before Trim Start.

parameters.label: Extend Right
parameters.name: textendright
parameters.description: ⊞  - Determines how the Point File In  TOP  handles animation positions that lie after the Trim End position. For example, if Trim End is set to 20, and the animation's current index is 25, the Extend Right menu determines how the movie position is calculated.

parameters.label: Hold
parameters.name: hold
parameters.description: Displays the last frame in the animation range (the frame specified by Trim End) for any position after Trim End.

parameters.label: Cycle
parameters.name: cycle
parameters.description: Loops the animation range continuously.

parameters.label: Mirror
parameters.name: mirror
parameters.description: Loops the animation range in a zig-zag pattern. For example, playing forwards from Trim End the movie will index will start decending towards Trim Start, at which point is will start climbing towards Trim End and continue to zig-zag (or mirror) the further the animation plays.

parameters.label: Black
parameters.name: black
parameters.description: Displays black frame for any animation position after Trim End.

parameters.label: Override  Sample Rate
parameters.name: overridesample
parameters.description: Turn On to change the sample rate of the movie. When loading an image sequence, use these parameters to set the playback speed for the sequence.

parameters.label: Sample Rate
parameters.name: samplerate
parameters.description: Set the sample rate for playback when 'Override  Sample Rate ' above is On.

parameters.label: Pre-Read Frames
parameters.name: prereadframes
parameters.description: Sets how many animation frames TouchDesigner reads ahead and stores in memory. The Point File In  TOP  will read and decode frames of the animation into CPU memory before they are used, this can eliminate pops or stutters in playback that occur from some frames taking too long to decode, other resources accessing the hard drive, or looping. When reading a sequence of files, having more Pre-Read Frames will allow multiple files to be decode at the same time. This allows playback of heavy file formats such as .exr in real-time, assuming the machine has enough CPU cores.

parameters.label: Frame Read Timeout
parameters.name: frametimeout
parameters.description: The time (in milliseconds) TouchDesigner will wait for a frame from the hard drive before giving up. If the Disk Read Timeout time is reached, that frame is simply skipped. This also works for network files that are downloaded via http://.

parameters.label: Frame Timeout Strategy
parameters.name: frametimeoutstrat
parameters.description: ⊞  - When on, if the Disk Read Timeout is reached TouchDesigner will use the latest available frame in place of the skipped frame.

parameters.label: Keep  Frame
parameters.name: keep
parameters.description: Keep showing the same frame that is currently being output.

parameters.label: Best for Playback
parameters.name: playback
parameters.description: Try to pick the best frame for playback. This may be a newer frame that what is shown, but not quite the frame that is requested.

parameters.label: Best for Seeking
parameters.name: seeking
parameters.description: Try to show any frame, either before or after the target frame. Good for when seeking the movie via a shuttle widget in a UI.

parameters.label: Always Load Initial  Frame
parameters.name: alwaysloadinitial
parameters.description: If this parameter is turned on, then for the first loaded frame the Frame Read Timeout will be ignored, and it will always wait for the first frame to ensure the node always starts up with a valid image.

parameters.label: File Open Timeout
parameters.name: opentimeout
parameters.description: The time (in milliseconds) TouchDesigner will wait for a file to open. If the Disk Open Timout is reached, the Point File In  TOP  will stop waiting and make its image all black, with a grey square in the bottom right corner. If the file still isn't opened the next time the  TOP  cooks, it'll wait again, and do the same. It'll keep doing this until the file is opened, or the open fails.

parameters.label: Async Upload to  GPU
parameters.name: asyncupload
parameters.description: When enabled, this will use OpenGL features to upload movie images to the  GPU  asynchronously. This will reduce the cook time of the Movie File In  TOP  considerably (in the performance monitor the lines that say "Uploading Image to  GPU " will go down to almost nothing). There is a  GPU  memory cost to using this feature however. It uses up another (Width * Height * 4 * Read Ahead Size) bytes of  GPU  memory. If you are having poor results with this feature, make sure your graphics drivers are up to date.

parameters.label: Update Image
parameters.name: updateimage
parameters.description: Image will not update when set to 0. Animation index will continue to move forward but the output image will not update.

parameters.label: Max Decode CPUs
parameters.name: maxdecodecpus
parameters.description: Limit the maximum number of CPUs that will be used to decode certain file codecs that are capable of multi-CPU decoding.

parameters.label: High Performance Read
parameters.name: highperfread
parameters.description: This option should be used when playing back files that require very high SSD read speeds. It greatly improves read performance in those cases. It should not be used for low resolution or low data rate files.

parameters.label: High Performance Read Factor
parameters.name: highperfreadfactor
parameters.description: When doing high performance reads, this parameter controls the size of the read operations that are done on disk. Whatever the largest operation the codec asks to be done, this is multiplied by the read factor and all subsequent reads will read that much data instead. This can result in higher throughput depending on the drives. For example if a request is made to read 1MB and the factor is set to 3, then instead the operations will read 3MB from the disk and the extra 2MB read will be ready for the next frame and will likely already have the next 2 frames available in CPU RAM.

parameters.label: Hardware Decode
parameters.name: hwdecode
parameters.description: Controls if this node should use hardware decoding via the Nvidia hardware decoder chip. You can check if hardware decoding is being used using the Info  CHOP , 'hardware_decode' channel. This parameter does nothing for Hap and NotchLC codecs, which are always hardware decoded.

parameters.label: Output  Resolution
parameters.name: outputresolution
parameters.description: ⊞  - quickly change the resolution of the  TOP 's data.

parameters.label: Use Input
parameters.name: useinput
parameters.description: Uses the input's resolution

parameters.label: Eighth
parameters.name: eighth
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: Quarter
parameters.name: quarter
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: Half
parameters.name: half
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: 2X
parameters.name: 2x
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: 4X
parameters.name: 4x
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: 8X
parameters.name: 8x
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: Fit  Resolution
parameters.name: fit
parameters.description: Grow or shrink the input resolution to fit this resolution, while keeping the aspect ratio the same.

parameters.label: Limit  Resolution
parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Limit the input resolution to be not larger than this resolution, while keeping the aspect ratio the same.

parameters.label: Custom  Resolution
parameters.name: custom
parameters.description: Directly control the width and height.

parameters.label: Resolution
parameters.name: resolution
parameters.description: ⊞  - Enabled only when the  Resolution  parameter is set to Custom  Resolution . Some Generators like Constant and Ramp do not use inputs and only use this field to determine their size. The drop down menu on the right provides some commonly used resolutions.

parameters.label: Resolution  Menu
parameters.name: resmenu
parameters.description: A drop-down menu with some commonly used resolutions.

parameters.label: Use Global Res Multiplier
parameters.name: resmult
parameters.description: Uses the Global  Resolution  Multiplier found in  Edit>Preferences>TOPs . This multiplies all the TOPs resolutions by the set amount. This is handy when working on computers with different hardware specifications. If a project is designed on a desktop workstation with lots of graphics memory, a user on a laptop with only 64MB VRAM can set the Global  Resolution  Multiplier to a value of half or quarter so it runs at an acceptable speed. By checking this checkbox on, this  TOP  is affected by the global multiplier.

parameters.label: Output Aspect
parameters.name: outputaspect
parameters.description: ⊞  - Sets the image aspect ratio allowing any textures to be viewed in any size. Watch for unexpected results when compositing TOPs with different aspect ratios. (You can define images with non-square pixels using xres, yres, aspectx, aspecty where xres/yres != aspectx/aspecty.)

parameters.label: Use Input
parameters.name: useinput
parameters.description: Uses the input's aspect ratio.

parameters.label: Resolution
parameters.name: resolution
parameters.description: Uses the aspect of the image's defined resolution (ie 512x256 would be 2:1), whereby each pixel is square.

parameters.label: Custom Aspect
parameters.name: custom
parameters.description: Lets you explicitly define a custom aspect ratio in the Aspect parameter below.

parameters.label: Aspect
parameters.name: aspect
parameters.description: ⊞  - Use when Output Aspect parameter is set to Custom Aspect.

parameters.label: Aspect Menu
parameters.name: armenu
parameters.description: A drop-down menu with some commonly used aspect ratios.

parameters.label: Input Smoothness
parameters.name: inputfiltertype
parameters.description: ⊞  - This controls pixel filtering on the input image of the  TOP .

parameters.label: Nearest Pixel
parameters.name: nearest
parameters.description: Uses nearest pixel or accurate image representation. Images will look jaggy when viewing at any zoom level other than Native  Resolution .

parameters.label: Interpolate Pixels
parameters.name: linear
parameters.description: Uses linear filtering between pixels. This is how you get  TOP  images in viewers to look good at various zoom levels, especially useful when using any Fill Viewer setting other than Native  Resolution .

parameters.label: Mipmap Pixels
parameters.name: mipmap
parameters.description: Uses   mipmap  filtering when scaling images. This can be used to reduce artifacts and sparkling in moving/scaling images that have lots of detail.

parameters.label: Fill  Viewer
parameters.name: fillmode
parameters.description: ⊞  - Determine how the  TOP  image is displayed in the viewer.

parameters.label: Use Input
parameters.name: useinput
parameters.description: Uses the same Fill Viewer settings as it's input.

parameters.label: Fill
parameters.name: fill
parameters.description: Stretches the image to fit the edges of the viewer.

parameters.label: Fit Horizontal
parameters.name: width
parameters.description: Stretches image to fit viewer horizontally.

parameters.label: Fit Vertical
parameters.name: height
parameters.description: Stretches image to fit viewer vertically.

parameters.label: Fit Best
parameters.name: best
parameters.description: Stretches or squashes image so no part of image is cropped.

parameters.label: Fit Outside
parameters.name: outside
parameters.description: Stretches or squashes image so image fills viewer while constraining it's proportions. This often leads to part of image getting cropped by viewer.

parameters.label: Native  Resolution
parameters.name: nativeres
parameters.description: Displays the native resolution of the image in the viewer.

parameters.label: Viewer Smoothness
parameters.name: filtertype
parameters.description: ⊞  - This controls pixel filtering in the viewers.

parameters.label: Nearest Pixel
parameters.name: nearest
parameters.description: Uses nearest pixel or accurate image representation. Images will look jaggy when viewing at any zoom level other than Native  Resolution .

parameters.label: Interpolate Pixels
parameters.name: linear
parameters.description: Uses linear filtering between pixels. Use this to get  TOP  images in viewers to look good at various zoom levels, especially useful when using any Fill Viewer setting other than Native  Resolution .

parameters.label: Mipmap Pixels
parameters.name: mipmap
parameters.description: Uses   mipmap  filtering when scaling images. This can be used to reduce artifacts and sparkling in moving/scaling images that have lots of detail. When the input is 32-bit float format, only nearest filtering will be used (regardless of what is selected).

parameters.label: Passes
parameters.name: npasses
parameters.description: Duplicates the operation of the  TOP  the specified number of times. For every pass after the first it takes the result of the previous pass and replaces the node's first input with the result of the previous pass. One exception to this is the  GLSL TOP  when using compute shaders, where the input will continue to be the connected  TOP 's image.

parameters.label: Channel Mask
parameters.name: chanmask
parameters.description: Allows you to choose which channels (R, G, B, or A) the  TOP  will operate on. All channels are selected by default.

parameters.label: Pixel Format
parameters.name: format
parameters.description: ⊞  - Format used to store data for each channel in the image (ie. R, G, B, and A). Refer to  Pixel Formats  for more information.

parameters.label: Use Input
parameters.name: useinput
parameters.description: Uses the input's pixel format.

parameters.label: 8-bit fixed (RGBA)
parameters.name: rgba8fixed
parameters.description: Uses 8-bit integer values for each channel.

parameters.label: sRGB 8-bit fixed (RGBA)
parameters.name: srgba8fixed
parameters.description: Uses 8-bit integer values for each channel and stores color in sRGB colorspace. Note that this does  not  apply an sRGB curve to the pixel values, it only stores them using an sRGB curve. This means more data is used for the darker values and less for the brighter values. When the values are read downstream they will be converted back to linear. For more information refer to  sRGB .

parameters.label: 16-bit float (RGBA)
parameters.name: rgba16float
parameters.description: Uses 16-bits per color channel, 64-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 32-bit float (RGBA)
parameters.name: rgba32float
parameters.description: Uses 32-bits per color channel, 128-bits per pixels.

parameters.label: 10-bit RGB, 2-bit Alpha, fixed (RGBA)
parameters.name: rgb10a2fixed
parameters.description: Uses 10-bits per color channel and 2-bits for alpha, 32-bits total per pixel.

parameters.label: 16-bit fixed (RGBA)
parameters.name: rgba16fixed
parameters.description: Uses 16-bits per color channel, 64-bits total per pixel.

parameters.label: 11-bit float (RGB), Positive Values Only
parameters.name: rgba11float
parameters.description: A RGB floating point format that has 11 bits for the Red and Green channels, and 10-bits for the Blue  Channel , 32-bits total per pixel (therefore the same memory usage as 8-bit RGBA). The Alpha channel in this format will always be 1. Values can go above one, but can't be negative. ie. the range is [0, infinite).

parameters.label: 8-bit fixed (Mono)
parameters.name: mono8fixed
parameters.description: Single channel, where RGB will all have the same value, and Alpha will be 1.0. 8-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 16-bit fixed (Mono)
parameters.name: mono16fixed
parameters.description: Single channel, where RGB will all have the same value, and Alpha will be 1.0. 16-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 16-bit float (Mono)
parameters.name: mono16float
parameters.description: Single channel, where RGB will all have the same value, and Alpha will be 1.0. 16-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 32-bit float (Mono)
parameters.name: mono32float
parameters.description: Single channel, where RGB will all have the same value, and Alpha will be 1.0. 32-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 8-bit fixed (RG)
parameters.name: rg8fixed
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, R and G have values, while B is 0 always and Alpha is 1.0. 8-bits per channel, 16-bits total per pixel.

parameters.label: 16-bit fixed (RG)
parameters.name: rg16fixed
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, R and G have values, while B is 0 always and Alpha is 1.0. 16-bits per channel, 32-bits total per pixel.

parameters.label: 16-bit float (RG)
parameters.name: rg16float
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, R and G have values, while B is 0 always and Alpha is 1.0. 16-bits per channel, 32-bits total per pixel.

parameters.label: 32-bit float (RG)
parameters.name: rg32float
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, R and G have values, while B is 0 always and Alpha is 1.0. 32-bits per channel, 64-bits total per pixel.

parameters.label: 8-bit fixed (A)
parameters.name: a8fixed
parameters.description: An Alpha only format that has 8-bits per channel, 8-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 16-bit fixed (A)
parameters.name: a16fixed
parameters.description: An Alpha only format that has 16-bits per channel, 16-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 16-bit float (A)
parameters.name: a16float
parameters.description: An Alpha only format that has 16-bits per channel, 16-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 32-bit float (A)
parameters.name: a32float
parameters.description: An Alpha only format that has 32-bits per channel, 32-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 8-bit fixed (Mono+Alpha)
parameters.name: monoalpha8fixed
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, one value for RGB and one value for Alpha. 8-bits per channel, 16-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 16-bit fixed (Mono+Alpha)
parameters.name: monoalpha16fixed
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, one value for RGB and one value for Alpha. 16-bits per channel, 32-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 16-bit float (Mono+Alpha)

parameters.description: A 2 channel format, one value for RGB and one value for Alpha. 16-bits per channel, 32-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 32-bit float (Mono+Alpha)
parameters.name: monoalpha32float
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, one value for RGB and one value for Alpha. 32-bits per channel, 64-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: resx

parameters.label: resy
parameters.description: Vertical resolution of the  TOP  in pixels.

parameters.label: aspectx
parameters.description: Horizontal aspect of the  TOP .

parameters.label: aspecty
parameters.description: Vertical aspect of the  TOP .

parameters.label: depth
parameters.description: Depth of 2D or 3D array if this  TOP  contains a 2D or 3D texture array.

parameters.label: gpu_memory_used
parameters.description: Total amount of texture memory used by this  TOP .

parameters.label: total_cooks
parameters.description: Number of times the operator has cooked since the process started.

parameters.label: cook_time

parameters.label: cook_frame

. * **Características clave:** * Cada punto anima el atributo `Phaser` de 0 a 1 en un ciclo, pero el valor de cada punto aumenta y llega a 1 en **momentos diferentes**. * Si el atributo de entrada tiene múltiples componentes, `Phase` también será multi-componente. * **Uso simple:** Útil para crear efectos de "onda" o "propagación" a través de un conjunto de puntos, donde la animación no ocurre en todos los puntos al mismo tiempo, sino que se desfasa. * **Point File In POP (POP de Entrada de Archivo de Puntos)** * **Función principal:** Carga **datos de puntos 3D** en los POPs desde archivos individuales o secuencias de archivos. * **Características clave:** * Soporta varios formatos de archivo como **.obj, .ply, .fits, .exr**, y archivos ASCII de puntos como **.xyz, .pts, .csv, .txt**. * Permite asignar campos del archivo (posición XYZ, normales, coordenadas de textura, color RGBA) a los **atributos** de POP. *
